newsitem.title: UK: Courts soars to new high on strong results.
newsitem.headline: Courts soars to new high on strong results.

text.p: Shares of British furniture retailer Courts Plc were marked at a record high on Thursday after the company announced encouraging half year results and said it planned to split its shares, analysts said.
Shares were quoted at a record 11.70 stg at 1227 GMT, up 185p from yesterday's close but no trades were recorded.
Pretax profits rose to 9.6 million stg, up from 8.75 million stg in the same period last year.
"They are very good results," said one marketmaker. "People are just digesting the news of the very positive figures."
The marketmaker said the shares had "found a level", but added that they may come off a little in the near future.
Courts said on Thursday morning it planned to split its shares and allot five new ordinary shares of 10 pence for every two ordinary shares of 25p. The move is subject to shareholder approval.
Analysts said the share split would be a positive move for the stock as it would increase liquidity. "It will make them (the shares) a little bit more tradeable," said the marketmaker.
Analysts also reacted favourably to the company's upbeat trading statement.

"In the British Isles turnover and profits continue to be encouraging ahead of the comparitive period, with the important winter sale still to come," said Courts chairman Paul Cohen. -- Nick Winning, London Newsroom + 44 171 542 7954
